title: Specification for Industrial Safety Helmets (Second Revision)
scope: Specifies physical, constructional, and performance requirements for industrial safety helmets intended to protect workers from falling objects and mechanical impact in industrial and construction environments.
description: Standard covering helmets made of non-metallic materials (such as HDPE, ABS, fiberglass) for shock absorption, penetration resistance, flammability, and electrical insulation in workplaces.
application: Construction sites, heavy manufacturing plants, refineries, mining surface works, and maintenance operations.

technical_requirements.harness_clearance: Vertical clearance between crown and harness: 25 mm to 50 mm
technical_requirements.chin_strap_width: Minimum 19 mm width with breakaway release

performance_requirements.shock_absorption: Transmitted force to headform shall not exceed 5.0 kN when subjected to 50 J impact energy
performance_requirements.penetration_resistance: 3 kg conical drop striker from 1 m height shall not pierce through shell or contact headform
performance_requirements.flammability: Shell material shall not continue burning for more than 5 seconds after flame removal

safety_requirements.electrical_insulation: Leakage current shall not exceed 1.2 mA at 1.2 kV AC (Proof test: 3 kV AC for 1 minute)

title: Protective Helmets for Two Wheeler Riders — Specification (Fourth Revision)

performance_requirements.impact_attenuation: Peak headform acceleration shall not exceed 300g (2940 m/s²) and HIC shall not exceed 2400 under 2.5 m drop test

safety_requirements.chin_strap_test: Retention strap width >= 20 mm; quick release mechanism under load
safety_requirements.audibility: Must not restrict rider acoustic perception significantly

certification.discrepancy_note: Official Indian Standard IS 694:2010 Fourth Revision defines rated voltages 'Up to and Including 450/750 V' (as affirmed by BIS Central Marks Department Circular dated 15 December 2014 and ETD 19). In contrast, the statutory Quality Control Order S.O. 189(E) dated 17 February 2003 (Schedule Serial 20, effective 17 August 2003) prescribes mandatory coverage for 'PVC insulated cables for working voltages up to and including 1100 V'. To bridge this statutory requirement, the BIS Product Manual PM/IS 694/5/March 2024 expands its title and certification scope to 'voltages up to and including 1100 V', granting ISI certification licenses up to 1100 V.
